title: Toric comparison for ideals, saturated blowups and smoothness
statement:
Let $M$ be a fine torsion-free monoscheme with a finite affine cover, let $k$ be a field, and put $X=k[M]$ [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. On each connected component use its torus $T$. Then:

(i) The map $I\mapsto k[I]$ is a bijection between coherent monoid ideals of $M$ and coherent $T$-equivariant ring ideals of $X$, allowing the empty monoid ideal to correspond to the zero ring ideal. It commutes with localization and pullback along monoscheme morphisms. The ideal $k[I]$ is the whole structure sheaf exactly when $I=\mathcal M$, and it is nonzero on a connected component exactly when $I$ is nonempty there.

(ii) For a coherent monoid ideal $I$ nonempty on every component, there is a canonical torus-equivariant identification $\operatorname{Bl}_{k[I]}(k[M])^\nu\simeq k[\operatorname{Bl}_I(M)^{\rm sat}]$, with the original dense torus unchanged. The saturated monoscheme blowup is again fine, torsion free and admits a finite affine cover. The identification respects localization and smooth pullback.

(iii) A smooth morphism $N\to M$ of fine monoschemes induces a smooth morphism $k[N]\to k[M]$ of schemes. If $k[M]\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth, then $M$ is smooth. In particular, if $k=\mathbf Q$ and $\mathbf Q[M]$ is regular, then every stalk of $M$ is $\mathbf N^r\oplus\mathbf Z^t$ for finite $r,t\ge0$.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.17--3.1.23, Lemmas 3.2.9, 3.2.12 and 3.2.15, Lemma 3.2.17 and Corollary 3.2.18, printed pp.101--105; regular-over-Q application in 3.2.19, p.106. No Stacks tag states this monoidal-geometric result.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-affine-toric-equivariant-ideals] on affine charts. Its inverse $J\mapsto\{p:e^p\in J\}$ commutes with restrictions, so the chart ideals glue uniquely to a coherent monoid ideal [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. Its extension formula gives arbitrary monoscheme pullback. Its zero and unit criteria on the charts give the componentwise nonvanishing and whole-ideal assertions in (i).

For (ii), choose finite chart ideal generators. They are nonempty: an empty chart ideal would have empty generic stalk, contrary to nonemptiness on its connected component. By [lem-trf-toric-blowup-chart-normalization], the normalized scheme charts are exactly the saturated monoid blowup charts of [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization], with identical transitions. Their restriction compatibility glues a canonical comparison over $k[M]$. The same lemma gives fine torsion-free charts, finitely many on our finite cover, equivariance, the identity on the original dense torus, and compatibility with localization.

For a smooth $N\to M$, choose smallest affine neighborhoods at every source point and at its image, using [lem-trf-monoscheme-smooth-local-charts]. Its restriction theorem identifies each section map with a product inclusion, and its realized product-chart theorem gives smoothness of the corresponding Spec map. The defining equations of the unique realization map [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization] identify its composite with the source chart embedding with this Spec map followed by the target chart embedding. Target chart embeddings are open immersions, hence smooth by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition]; composition is smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-composition]. The smallest-neighborhood realization charts cover by [lem-trf-monoscheme-smooth-local-charts]; [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source] therefore proves smoothness of the whole realization map. This part is implemented in realizationMap_smooth. Smooth-pullback compatibility for the still-open blowup comparison uses [lem-trf-saturated-blowup-product-charts]: on these same product charts both blowups and their comparison are pullbacks, and the overlap compatibilities glue their maps and commuting squares.

source.place: VIII 3.1.16, 3.1.23, 3.2.12(i), 3.2.17--3.2.18; original steps 6--7. Current-base repair: Stacks Tags 01VC (lemma-open-immersion-smooth) and 01VA (lemma-composition-smooth), via the existing composition nodes.

proof.text: Suppose $k[M]$ is smooth. Restrict to the smallest affine neighborhoods from [lem-trf-monoscheme-smooth-local-charts], using [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source]. By [lem-trf-smooth-toric-saturated-sharp-reduction], each section monoid is $P\simeq R\oplus\mathbf Z^t$ with $R$ fine saturated sharp and its toric vertex local ring regular. The finite atom generating set and its cotangent dimension are given by [lem-trf-sharp-monoid-vertex-cotangent]. For this same splitting and vertex, apply [lem-trf-toric-vertex-dimension-freeness], giving $R\simeq\mathbf N^r$. Since these section monoids are the stalks, every stalk is $\mathbf N^r\oplus\mathbf Z^t$. By [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization], these stalk forms mean that $M$ is smooth.

source.place: VIII proof of 3.2.12(ii), pp.104--105; original steps 8--12.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-toric-realization-finite-type] to obtain local finite type of the rational realization structure morphism; its torsion-free and finite-cover hypotheses are exactly those on $M$. The regular-scheme hypothesis supplies the upstream stalkwise regularity predicate. The field $\operatorname{ULift}\mathbf Q$ is perfect, so [lem-trf-regular-perfect-field-smooth] gives smoothness of this structure morphism. Apply isSmooth_of_realization_smooth from the preceding step to get exactly the stated stalk forms. This proof introduces no nonemptiness assumption or rank restriction.

I : IdealFamily M, IsCoherentIdeal I ∧ ringIdeal k I = J) ∧ (∀ (I I' : IdealFamily M), IsCoherentIdeal I → IsCoherentIdeal I' → ringIdeal k I = ringIdeal k I' → I = I') ∧ ringIdeal k (emptyIdeal M) = ⊥ ∧ (∀ I : IdealFamily M, IsCoherentIdeal I → (ringIdeal k I = ⊤ ↔ I = wholeIdeal M) ∧ ∀ C : ToricComponent M, (ringIdeal k I).comap (componentι k C) ≠ ⊥ ↔ ∃ x : M.space, ConnectedComponents.mk x = C.component ∧ (idealStalk I x).Nonempty) ∧ (∀ (N : Fine.{u}) (f : Hom N M) (I : IdealFamily M), IsCoherentIdeal I → IsCoherentIdeal (pullbackIdeal f I) ∧ ringIdeal k (pullbackIdeal f I) = (ringIdeal k I).comap (realizationMap k f))
